claims.text: Psychological interventions delivered via smartphone result in significantly greater reductions in total anxiety scores compared to control conditions.
There was no evidence of publication bias in the meta-analysis of smartphone interventions for anxiety.
Smartphone interventions produce significantly greater reductions in anxiety compared to waitlist or inactive control conditions.
Smartphone interventions produce significantly greater reductions in anxiety compared to active control conditions.

evidence.description: Significantly greater reductions in total anxiety scores were observed from smartphone interventions than control conditions (g=0.325, 95% C.I.=0.17-0.48, p<0.01)
Meta-analysis showed no evidence of publication bias among included RCTs.
Effect sizes from smartphone interventions were significantly greater when compared to waitlist/inactive controls (g=0.45, 95% C.I.=0.30-0.61, p<0.01)
Effect sizes from smartphone interventions were significant compared to active control conditions (g=0.19, 95% C.I.=0.07-0.31, p=0.003)

methodologies.name: Systematic Review and Random-Effects Meta-Analysis
methodologies.description: A systematic search of major electronic databases conducted in November 2016 identified 9 eligible RCTs evaluating smartphone-delivered psychological interventions on anxiety using random-effects meta-analyses to calculate Hedges' g.

limitations.text: The extent to which smartphone interventions can match (or exceed) the efficacy of recognised treatments for anxiety has yet to be established.

future_work.text: Develop pragmatic methods for implementing smartphone-based support for people with anxiety.
Compare the efficacy of smartphone interventions to standard face-to-face psychological care.
